addons.official_updates: Say once when a newer version of an official add-on you have is out; it's never updated by itself.
addons.on: Load the add-ons you added by link (`kurooto addons add`); off, none load from the next start.
agent_plan.name: The name of Kurooto's own calendar for the time blocks it plans with you.
agent_plan.remind_min: Minutes before each planned block for Google's pop-up reminder; 0: none.
agents.export: Which other AI programs get your skills as slash commands, so /journal works there too.
agents.prefix: A prefix put before every skill copied into your other AI programs, e.g. `k-` for /k-journal.
agents.scripts: Scripts of your own the AI programs may run during a request (full paths).
alarm.bedtime: With an alarm set, no calls from this time until it rings; none uses the night hours' start.
alarm.daily: A wake-up time that rings every day (on the days below) unless you set another for that morning.
alarm.days: The days the daily alarm rings.
alarm.keep_awake: Keep this computer awake before the alarm so the day's plan is drafted in time.
alarm.notes: After the wake-up call, today's plan (or what you said on the call) goes into your daily note.
alarm.open_page: When the alarm rings, the morning page opens on this computer (if it's awake).
alarm.prep_min: Minutes before the alarm that your AI drafts the day's plan into today's daily note.
alarm.reason: What the wake-up call says it's for.
alarm.retries: How many more times the alarm rings if you don't answer (5 minutes apart).
alarm.snooze_min: Minutes a snoozed alarm waits before it rings again.
alarm.suggest: Before your usual bedtime with no alarm set, one message offering your usual wake-up time.
ask.expire_hours: Hours an unanswered question stays open before it expires (unless its asker set another time).
ask.keep_days: Days answered and expired questions are kept before they're forgotten.
autostart.when: When Kurooto starts: when you log in, or (Linux with systemd) when the computer starts, before anyone logs in.
availability.absence_days: After this many days with nothing from you, one gentle "all good?" message.
availability.focus_keyword: A calendar event with this word in its title is focus time: messages and calls wait.
availability.learn_morning: The check-in day, the morning message and "Time to start" follow your learned hours.
availability.learn_night: Move the night hours to when you're actually quiet, learned from three weeks of your activity, with Undo.
availability.night: The night hours: when calls are held, and whether only a night with an alarm set counts.
availability.night.alarm_only: Hold calls at night only on nights you've set a wake-up alarm.
availability.night.enabled: No calls during the night hours.
availability.nocall_calendar: Part of a calendar's name: every event in such a calendar holds calls.
availability.nocall_keyword: A calendar event with this word in its title holds calls while it's on.
awake.lid: Linux: keep running with the lid closed while plugged in.
backups.confidential_mail: Include confidential mail summarised on this computer (the Mail digest's local mode).
backups.folder: Where the backup zips go: an external drive or a cloud-synced folder.
backups.index: Include the notes brain's index (big, but slow to rebuild).
backups.keep: How many backup zips to keep; Kurooto removes only its own older zips.
backups.memory: Include the memory ledger (encrypted: it opens only where its key is).
backups.notes: Include your notes folder in the backup.
backups.secrets: Include passwords and keys (bot token, API keys, sign-ins): anyone with the zip can use them.
books.after_read: A command of yours run after each book is read, with its subject and id added.
books.at: When the night's book reading begins (on the charger).
books.brain: Index each book's text into the notes brain, so search by meaning finds it.
books.brain_source: Which notes-brain source the book text goes into; empty is the default one.
books.dpi: How sharp the page pictures are for reading scanned pages.
books.duplicates: A book that's the same file as one already read is linked to it, not read again.
books.folder: Your own folder for books, with a subfolder per subject.
books.gemini: Pages nothing on this computer can read go to Google's Gemini as pictures.
books.gemini_model: Which Gemini model reads scanned book pages, when `books.gemini` is on.
books.latex: Which pages the vision model reads for LaTeX: only ones whose maths came out in pieces, all, or never.
books.max_mb: PDFs bigger than this (MB) are left alone.
books.ocr: Who reads scanned pages: Tesseract, a vision model on this computer, either, or nobody.
books.ocr_lang: Tesseract's languages for scanned pages, e.g. `eng+deu`.
books.until: When the night's reading stops; it carries on the next night from that page.
brain.agy: How Kurooto talks to the agy program.
brain.agy.io_mode: How Kurooto talks to the agy program: through a pipe, or a pseudo-terminal.
brain.base_urls: Another address for an AI's service, in place of its preset.
brain.classify: Who decides how hard a request is (and so how much effort it gets).
brain.claude: Claude Code kept running for a conversation.
brain.claude.session: Keep Claude Code running between turns of a conversation, so each message doesn't start it again.
brain.claude.session_idle_min: Minutes a kept Claude Code waits for your next message before it closes.
brain.claude_accounts: Your extra Claude accounts, each its own AI you can pick (`claude:<name>`).
brain.effort_map: Effort changes Dreaming learned for your requests, e.g. low ones run at medium.
brain.fallback: Which AI takes over when your main one can't answer, in order.
brain.fallback_first: Effort levels at which your first stand-in AI is tried before the main one (learned by Dreaming).
brain.fallback_on: What makes a request move on to the stand-in AI: a limit, a sign-in problem or a timeout.
brain.main: The AI that answers your requests and does the bigger tasks.
brain.models: Which model each AI uses at each effort level, where you want other than its preset.
brain.timeout_min: Minutes a request may run before it's stopped, for quick, normal and hard requests.
brain.timeout_min.high: Minutes a hard request may run before it's stopped.
brain.timeout_min.low: Minutes a quick request may run before it's stopped.
brain.timeout_min.medium: Minutes a normal request may run before it's stopped.
calendar.class_calendars: Calendars whose events are classes: they hold calls and get the after-class question.
calendar.days: How many days ahead Kurooto reads your calendar.
calendar.holiday_calendars: Calendars whose all-day events are holidays (no classes).
calendar.mask_private: Private events show only as "Busy (private)": no title, place or description kept.
calendar.no_calls_in_events: No calls while a calendar event is on.
calendar.nocall_events: Which events hold calls: every timed one, or only those you tagged.
calendar.private_keyword: An event with this word in its title or description is private.
calendar.refresh: How often the calendar is read again.
calendar.remind_min: Minutes before each timed event for a reminder; 0 is off.
calendar.shared_offer: A subscribed calendar's deadlines and exams are offered with an Add button each.
calls.chat_edit: Edit your own messages in the app's chat for 15 minutes after sending.
calls.chat_files_inline: Files in the app's chat show inline and open in the app.
calls.chat_sessions: Separate chats in the phone app, each its own conversation whose context carries over.
calls.chat_titles: How a new chat gets its title: its first words, or a short title from your AI.
calls.later_min: Minutes until it calls back after you tap Later on a ringing call.
calls.lessons_max: How many lessons from past calls every call is told; a repeat replaces the older one.
calls.live_model: The Gemini Live model calls try first.
calls.live_models: Other Live models to try, in order, when the first one is down.
calls.notes_repo: Your notes' repository on GitHub, so calls can read whole notes while this computer is off.
calls.ntfy_server: The push server the phone app listens on. Change it only if you run your own.
calls.persona: Your own words on how calls should sound, such as "be brief and a bit cheeky".
calls.realert_min: Minutes after the first ring that an unanswered call rings again.
calls.review: After every call, an AI request looks back at it: does what slipped through and keeps lessons.
calls.review_brain: Which AI does the look back after a call; empty is your main one.
calls.review_effort: How hard the look back after a call thinks.
calls.ring_s: Seconds a call rings before it counts as missed (a wake-up call rings 5 minutes).
calls.text_model: The Gemini model that answers turn-by-turn calls (here, or on your call line while the computer is off).
calls.today: Your phone app's Today screen and its copy of your alarm, kept up to date from this computer.
calls.turn_brain: Who answers turn-by-turn calls on your computer: Gemini with your key, or a local model.
calls.views: Systems and the Notes map in the phone app: your notes' titles and links, and each feature's health.
calls.views_being: Show the being in the phone app's Views: the dashboard's own body of Kurooto, drawn on the phone from a sealed copy.
calls.views_brain: Show the Brain console in the phone app's Views (the Brain choice), sealed for your phone like Systems and the Notes map.
calls.views_links: The most links on the phone's Notes map (a book's "Seen in" links go first).
calls.views_notes: The most notes on the phone's Notes map (best linked first).
calls.voice: Which Gemini Live voice calls speak in; empty is Google's default.
calls.voice_by_kind: The voice mode for one kind of call, e.g. the alarm always on the phone's speech.
calls.voice_by_model: A voice for each Live model, where a model doesn't know the one in `calls.voice`.
calls.voice_mode: How calls listen and speak: Gemini Live, your phone's own speech turn by turn, or Live with the phone as backup.
calls.worker: Your call line's name, address and version (set by Kurooto when it's deployed).
calls.worker.name: Your call line's name on Cloudflare (set when it's deployed).
calls.worker.url: Your call line's address (set when it's deployed).
calls.worker.version: The version of your call line that's deployed (set by Kurooto).
capture.delay_min: Minutes after a class ends before it asks what happened in it.
capture.skip_subjects: Never ask after these subjects' classes.
capture.study_log: Your AI turns your after-class answer into a lecture note.
capture.subjects: Ask only after these subjects' classes; empty asks after every subject.
cases.button: A Wrong button under replies to plain-English requests (`/wrong` works either way).
cases.fallthroughs: Keep short requests no instant request understood, to learn from later.
cases.keep_days: Cases you didn't make test cases are forgotten after this many days (0: `privacy.keep_days`, else 30).
cases.learn: A test case may teach its phrasing, but only if every test case that passed still passes.
cases.learn_rephrased: The same not-understood phrasing twice followed by the same request: it's learned.
cases.review: When the monthly list of most common not-understood phrasings may come.
cases.review_days: Days at least between two such lists.
chat.context_line: Each message carries one line for your AI on how it came: typed where, a call, stepped away from the desk.
chat.context_places: Add your phone's last saved place and the Wi-Fi's name you gave it to that line.
checkins.ai_notes: After a check-in call, your AI writes your journal and study logs from what you said.
checkins.asleep_defers: With check-ins by call and an alarm set, the night check-in waits for the morning once you've gone to bed.
checkins.by_call: Check-ins come as a call (a missed call falls back to Telegram).
checkins.day_starts: When a check-in day begins, so a night check-in at 00:30 still counts for the evening before.
checkins.journal: Each check-in's answer goes into your journal.
checkins.learn_times: A check-in you keep moving or answering late moves to when you actually do it, with Undo.
checkins.reflect: The evening check-in lists up to three things today's records show you did, and asks what's first tomorrow.
checkins.times: When each check-in comes: evening, night and midday (none: that one is off).
checkins.times.evening: When the evening check-in comes: the day in review.
checkins.times.midday: When the midday check-in comes (off unless you set a time).
checkins.times.night: When the night check-in comes, just before bed (off unless you set a time).
classroom_notes.at: When new Classroom posts are fetched into your notes.
classroom_notes.backfill_days: How far back (days) it looks; older posts not edited since are left alone.
classroom_notes.files: Download the Drive files attached to posts and read their text into your notes.
classroom_notes.folders: Which notes folder each course goes into, where Kurooto's own pick is wrong.
classroom_notes.max_file_mb: Attached files bigger than this (MB) are only linked, not downloaded.
classroom_notes.skip: Courses to leave out, by words from their names (`/classnotes skip` fills it).
commitments.hooks: Words of yours that start a hold: "gym" alone holds calls for 90 minutes.
commitments.items: Your regular commitments (the gym, a shift, a standup), each on its days and hours.
commitments.no_calls: No calls while a commitment is on.
date_offers.remind_min: An event you tap Add on (from a photo, mail or a shared calendar) is reminded this long before.
deadlines.call: The urgent nudge is a call, when Phone calls is on (a message when no call fits before it).
deadlines.exam_mode_days: Days before a quiz or exam that exam mode starts (more practice, revision); 0 turns it off.
deadlines.from_calendar: Calendar events that look like deadlines or exams join the deadline list.
deadlines.from_photos: Send a photo with the caption "dates" and its dates come back as buttons to add.
deadlines.from_term_note: The term note's quizzes, exams and deadlines join the deadline list.
deadlines.horizon_days: How far ahead recurring quizzes become dated deadlines, in days.
deadlines.max_files: The most notes read when looking for deadlines (notes over 1 MB are skipped).
deadlines.meeting_brief: The evening before a meeting with a project's person: a short brief of where things stand.
deadlines.overdue_check: After a deadline's due time: "Overdue?" with Done / New date / Drop.
deadlines.ping_h: Hours before a deadline that its first nudge comes (one message, with Done / Not mine / Snooze).
deadlines.plan_h: How far ahead "due soon" looks, in hours: the morning plan, /status and calls.
deadlines.recurring: Recurring quizzes (from kurooto/recurring.md in your notes) become dated deadlines.
deadlines.scan_notes: Find deadlines in your notes: dated `- [ ]` tasks.
deadlines.skip_notes: Notes or folders the deadline scan leaves alone.
deadlines.tick_notes: Done ticks the `- [ ]` line in your notes when the deadline came from one.
deadlines.urgent_h: Hours before a deadline that it's urgent: a call (with Phone calls) or an urgent message.
doubts.before_min: Open doubts for a subject come this many minutes before its next class.
doubts.recent_h: A doubt that names no subject is filed under the class that's on, or ended this many hours ago.
drafts.max_comments: The most comments "Check my draft" puts on one draft.
drafts.note_block: For checked notes, the comments also go into a block in the matching lecture note.
drafts.recent_minutes: "Check this" right after you sent a file checks that file, if it came this recently (minutes).
dreaming.consolidate: Ask about things it remembers twice or that disagree: Keep A / Keep B / Both true.
dreaming.consolidate_ai: A second opinion on near misses: a model here, your AI, or none.
dreaming.consolidate_max: The most such questions in one morning message; the rest wait.
dreaming.curious: Mention a topic you asked about 3+ times this week that has no note, with Make a stub.
dreaming.fold: In the morning message, offer lasting things you said for your profile (Keep / Not that).
dreaming.fold_ai: A second look at what the rules found for your profile: a model here, your AI, or none.
dreaming.fold_max: The most profile suggestions in one morning message.
dreaming.loose_ends: The morning message also lists loose ends: open doubts, unlinked notes, broken links, tasks past due.
dreaming.never_tune: Kinds of message it never tunes (besides the alarm, your reminders and calls, deadlines under 12 hours).
dreaming.propose_prompts: Offer a fix for a skill that keeps going wrong, as a proposal you apply or not.
dreaming.resurface: Bring back one thing from the past: a note or quiz subject from 10-30 days ago, or an anniversary.
dreaming.self_check: Each morning, replay your test cases and say which ones went wrong since yesterday.
dreaming.tune_effort: Each night, replay your requests and tune the effort they get (one change, with Undo).
dreaming.tune_fallbacks: Each night, check which AI did best at each effort and let that one go first (with Undo).
dreaming.tune_margin: How much better a change must score in the replay than leaving things as they are.
dreaming.tune_messages: Each night, replay the messages it sent you and tune when they come (one change, with Undo).
dreaming.tune_sizing: Each night, adjust Start-by's sizes to how long your deadlines really took.
dreaming.when: When the morning message comes ("While you slept"), covering everything since the last one.
drive_upload.big_files: A file too big for Telegram (over 50 MB) comes as a Drive link instead of failing.
drive_upload.folder: The Google Drive folder files go to.
drive_upload.temp_days: Days a too-big-for-Telegram upload is kept in your Drive before it's deleted; 0 keeps them.
exam_season.alarm_check: Every night of the exam period: will tomorrow's alarm ring?
exam_season.block_min: Minutes in one revision block (one topic each).
exam_season.budget: During exams, only deadlines, quizzes and the alarm come in the day; the rest waits for the evening.
exam_season.debrief: After each exam, a two-minute debrief that goes into the subject's course note.
exam_season.eve: The evening before an exam, a checklist: where it is, your seat, calculator, ID card.
exam_season.eve_at: When the evening-before question can come.
exam_season.exam_min: How long an exam lasts, in minutes (no calls then; the debrief comes half an hour after).
exam_season.hold_updates: During exams, updates that aren't critical wait until the exams are over.
exam_season.leave_alarm: On an exam day, an alarm to leave (a call with Phone calls, else a message).
exam_season.leave_min: Minutes before the exam the leave alarm goes, unless you say a time ("leave 8:10").
exam_season.night_at: When the nightly alarm check runs.
exam_season.no_calls: Hold every call while an exam is on.
exam_season.quiz_call_at: When a quiz call you picked rings the evening before an exam.
exam_season.quizzes: Treat quizzes and tests outside an exam period as exams too.
exam_season.revision: A revision plan before each exam: its topics ranked and fitted into your free time (/revise).
exam_season.revision_ask: Each evening: did you cover today's revision topics? (Counts like a quiz answer.)
exam_season.revision_days: Days before each exam that the revision plan starts.
exam_season.revision_share: The share of your free time (in %) revision blocks may take.
face.addons: What add-ons may do with Face presence: see who's in view, and keep the camera looking while you type.
face.addons.hold: Let an add-on keep the camera looking while you type (never past a pause, the night, a call or a switch).
face.addons.known_guests: An add-on may say that everyone else in view is someone it knows: they get the short greeting instead of none.
face.addons.watch: Let an add-on see who's in view: each face's place, size and numbers, in memory only, never a picture.
face.away: Notice when you leave the desk, and hold what Kurooto would start by itself until you're back.
face.away.after_min: No sign of you (your face or the keyboard) this long means you've left, in minutes.
face.away.hold_calls: While you're away, calls Kurooto would start by itself wait for you (up to the longest wait below).
face.away.hold_desktop: Hold desktop pop-ups and spoken answers until you're back at the desk.
face.away.hold_max_min: The longest a call waits while you're away, in minutes.
face.away.on: Notice when you leave the desk and come back.
face.away.places_close_camera: While your phone is out, keep the camera closed.
face.away.report_others: While you're away, note the times someone else's face was in view at your desk, and tell you once when you're back.
face.away.use_places: Your phone leaving a place you saved marks you away from the desk at once.
face.camera: Which camera Face presence uses and the picture size it asks for.
face.camera.device: The camera to use: empty for the first ordinary one (infrared ones are skipped), or a number or part of its name.
face.camera.height: The picture height asked of the camera.
face.camera.width: The picture width asked of the camera (it may give another).
face.camera.yaw_offset_deg: How far beside the camera's lens the spot you look at sits, in degrees (+: to your right); look to talk centres there.
face.greet: The greeting when you sit down: when, how often, what it says, and whether it then listens.
face.greet.addons: An add-on may add one short line of its own to the desk greeting.
face.greet.after_absent_min: Greet you only after you've been away at least this long, in minutes.
face.greet.gap_min: The fewest minutes between two greetings.
face.greet.listen_s: How long that conversation stays open with nothing said, in seconds.
face.greet.on: Greet you by voice when you arrive at the desk.
face.greet.records: With Brain on, each greeting is one of its decision records, closed by whether you answered it.
face.greet.say: What the greeting tells you: what's next today, what's waiting, deadlines in 24 h, what was held while you were away.
face.greet.talk: After the greeting, listen for a reply without its name being said.
face.greet.tell_ai: When you answer the desk greeting, your AI is told what it had just said, so "yes" carries on from it.
face.greet.with_others: When someone else is in view too: skip the greeting, say just "Welcome back.", or the full greeting.
face.learn: Refining your face template slowly from times it was very sure it was you.
face.learn.every_h: At most one new sample this often, in hours.
face.learn.from_voice: A turn Voice ID is sure is your voice, with only your face in view, may teach the face model too.
face.learn.margin: How far above your threshold a frame's score must be before it may refine your template.
face.learn.max: At most this many learned samples (the oldest goes first); the enrolled ones are never replaced.
face.learn.on: Slowly refine your face template from times it was very sure it was you (never unsure ones), with Undo.
face.light_sense: Read the room's light from the camera's frames, as one smoothed number, for Brain and add-ons.
face.recognise: How sure it must be that a face is yours, and how far away a face may be.
face.recognise.frames: Recognised in this many of the last 4 frames means you're here.
face.recognise.min_face_px: Faces smaller than this many pixels are ignored: too far away to judge.
face.recognise.strictness: How rarely a stranger may pass: loose (1 in 100 frames), normal (1 in 1,000) or strict (1 in 10,000).
face.recognise.threshold: 0 uses the calibrated threshold; a score from 0 to 1 overrides it (never below 0.363).
face.track: Follow every face in view while the camera is open, so the being's eye can look at whoever is there.
face.track.fps: How many times a second it looks for faces while following them (1 to 15).
face.track.on: While the camera is open, follow every face in view (where it is and how much it moves) for the being's eye.
face.watch: When the camera looks: how often, on battery, at night, and with the screen locked.
face.watch.fps: How many pictures a second it checks while waiting for you (0.2 to 2).
face.watch.fps_battery: Frames a second while the computer is on battery.
face.watch.idle_s: Seconds with no keyboard or mouse before the camera looks; while you type it doesn't need to.
face.watch.look_fps: While Voice listens for a look (voice.listen.look_to_talk), the camera checks at least this many pictures a second.
face.watch.night: Also look during the night hours (Availability's night); off pauses it at night.
face.watch.when_locked: Also look while the screen is locked; off pauses it while locked.
files.folder: A folder for files outside your notes (course files, PDFs); empty keeps them inside the notes.
files.links: How notes link to files outside the notes folder.
finder.folders: The folders Find files indexes and searches (`/find add <folder>` adds one).
finder.max_files: The most files Find files indexes.
finder.read_mb: Files bigger than this (MB) have their name indexed but not their text.
gbrain.agy_mcp: Your own GBrain: agy gets its MCP tools too (you're asked first).
gbrain.checkup: A weekly checkup of the brain; a message only when something needs a look.
gbrain.checkup_ignore: Checkup findings starting with these words aren't reported.
gbrain.checkup_line: Once a week, one line on how the notes brain is (read only).
gbrain.contradictions: The brain's last contradictions report joins Dreaming's morning section, with Keep A / Keep B.
gbrain.course_pages: Nightly, each course page gets its key concepts and a dated timeline, in Kurooto's own block.
gbrain.embeddings: How the notes brain makes its search-by-meaning index: a model here, Google's, or keywords only.
gbrain.exe: Your own GBrain: your gbrain program; empty uses the one on your PATH.
gbrain.home: Your own GBrain: its GBRAIN_HOME folder; empty uses GBrain's default.
gbrain.managed: Kurooto runs its own notes brain; off, it uses a GBrain you already run.
gbrain.mcp_surface: What your brain's MCP server offers agy: everything, a starter set, or only verbs.
gbrain.nightly: When the brain's nightly timelines and upkeep run.
gbrain.source: Your own GBrain: the source that is your notes folder, kept in step every 15 minutes.
gbrain.sync: How often your notes are read into the notes brain.
gbrain.timelines: Nightly, dated log lines in your notes become each note's timeline (`/timeline <note>`).
gbrain.upkeep: Nightly upkeep of the brain (links, facts, the index), light steps only; waits for the charger.
gbrain.upkeep_steps: Which upkeep steps run (GBrain's own phase names); empty: the light ones.
google.accounts: The names of your signed-in Google accounts; "main" is the one you signed in with first.
google.agent_calendar: Permission for Kurooto's own "Agent plan" calendar (it can't see your others).
google.calendar_read: Permission to read your calendars (Google Calendar), read-only.
google.classroom: Read Classroom: courses, assignments and announcements, for deadlines.
google.classroom_every: How often Classroom is checked for new deadlines.
google.classroom_notes: Permission for Classroom → notes: materials and attached Drive files, read-only.
google.digest_email: Permission to send the mail digest to your own inbox (send only).
google.drive_upload: Permission to put files you send yourself into a Kurooto folder in Drive (its own files only).
google.endpoints: Google's service addresses. Leave them alone.
google.endpoints.auth: Google's sign-in address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.calendar: Google Calendar's API address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.classroom: Google Classroom's API address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.drive: Google Drive's API address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.drive_upload: Google Drive's upload address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.gmail: Gmail's API address. Leave it alone.
google.endpoints.token: Google's token address. Leave it alone.
google.gmail_drafts: Allow `/draft` to save drafts in your Gmail (one more sign-in: Google calls it a restricted permission).
google.mail_digest: Permission for the mail digest: read Gmail, read-only.
google.reply_drafts: Permission for reply drafts in Gmail, sent only when you tap Send.
google.use: Which of your Google accounts each feature uses; unset means main.
google_calendar.skip: Google calendars to leave out, by any part of their name.
handwritten.cloud: With no model on this computer, Gemini reads the pages; off, they wait for a model here.
handwritten.dpi: How sharp the pictures of handwritten pages are when they're read.
handwritten.every: How often the handwritten-notes folder is checked for new scans.
handwritten.folder: Where scans of handwritten pages land to be read.
handwritten.into: Where the written-out notes go, inside your notes folder.
handwritten.keep_original: Keep a copy of the scan next to the note, or link to where it already is.
handwritten.link: Link each written-out note to its lecture, course page and concept notes.
handwritten.local: A model on this computer reads the pages when there is one.
handwritten.local_model: An Ollama model of your choice that reads pictures; empty uses Local AI models' pick.
handwritten.max_pages: The most pages written out per PDF.
handwritten.model: Which Gemini model reads handwriting when it's used.
handwritten.pdf_hours: When the model on this computer reads PDFs (on the charger); empty: any time.
hardware.extra_models: Ollama models of your own to install, past what suits this computer.
hardware.extra_prereqs: Other programs Kurooto should install for you, by id.
hardware.force_profile: Use another hardware profile's models than the one detected for this computer.
health.auto_fix: Try a safe fix before telling you (never a sync: that one waits for your tap).
health.on: The daily health pass: it checks what matters and tells you only when something needs you.
health.when: When the daily health pass runs; tonight's alarm is checked then.
infer.aliases: "By POTA I mean Physics of the Atmosphere" gives that subject a short name.
infer.classes: "Every Monday at 9 I have a <subject> lab" adds a class to your timetable.
infer.commitments: "Every Tuesday at 7pm I go to the gym" adds a commitment (it holds calls like a class).
infer.meetings: "Met X today" adds a dated line to that project's Meetings; a meeting ahead becomes a deadline.
infer.on: Set things up from what you say in the chat and the journal ("every Monday at 9 I have a lab"), each with Undo.
infer.projects: "I got a project under Prof X" makes a project note with them and a Meetings section.
infer.quizzes: "There's a quiz on Linear Algebra every Monday" adds a row to the recurring quizzes table.
infer.short_names: "LA" becomes Linear Algebra's short name after two messages use it (when it fits only that subject).
infer.sweep: One pass over your chats and journal for such sentences: once when first on, then nightly on what's new.
infer.sweep_ai: A line the rules can't read: a model here restates it, your AI does, or it's skipped.
infer.sweep_days: How far back (days) the first pass over your chats and journal reads.
integrate.at: When the night's reading starts (it carries on batch after batch).
integrate.auto_merge: Look-alike concept notes that are clearly one concept merge by themselves (Undo in the morning line).
integrate.auto_merge_min: How alike two notes must be (0.92 to 1) to merge without asking.
integrate.batch_pages: About how many pages go into one request.
integrate.commit: One git commit per batch, when your notes folder is a repository.
integrate.duplicates: Each morning, up to three pairs of look-alike concept notes: Merge / Keep both / Add alias.
integrate.duplicates_all: Each morning, also ask about notes of any kind that are copies of each other, old ones included.
integrate.duplicates_per_day: How many pairs of copied notes it asks about in a day, at most.
integrate.embeddings: How related notes are found by meaning: a model here, Google's, or not at all.
integrate.garden: A daily second pass that links the notes the reading touched and notes nothing links to yet.
integrate.garden_at: When the daily second pass runs (`/graph garden` runs it now).
integrate.garden_per_day: The most notes in the daily second pass.
integrate.max_cost_per_night: With a paid API key: the most a night's reading may cost, in US dollars.
integrate.notation: A Notation table when a second source writes a concept differently.
integrate.order: Which books first: the smallest (most books done soonest) or by name.
integrate.per_night: How many batches a night: fitted to your AI's plan, or a number you set as a hard ceiling.
integrate.price_per_mtok: An API key's prices per million tokens, for the night's cost estimate when it reports none.
integrate.price_per_mtok.in: An API key that reports no cost: its price per million input tokens (USD), for the estimate.
integrate.price_per_mtok.out: An API key that reports no cost: its price per million output tokens (USD), for the estimate.
integrate.rerank: A local model judges which notes belong together (a graphics card helps).
integrate.rerank_model: Which local model does that judging; empty uses this computer's helper model.
integrate.roles: Which AI does the bulk reading, and which takes the second look.
integrate.roles.bulk: The AI that does the bulk reading; empty is chosen for you.
integrate.roles.check: The AI that takes the second look at doubtful answers; empty is chosen for you.
integrate.share_pct: The most of a subscription's usage window (or a free key's day) the reading may take, in %.
integrate.sources: What's read into the graph: books, Classroom files, handwritten notes, repositories, reference files.
integrate.summary: One line each morning about what the reading changed.
jobs.header: A first line on each answer naming the AI and repeating what you asked.
jobs.plan_line: Before a long answer, one short line saying what it's about to do and roughly how long.
jobs.receipt: One quiet line under each answer: which AI, effort, time, limit used and what it did.
jobs.stuck_min: Minutes a request may sit with no AI at work and no program running before the watchdog stops it.
keep.ask: On day 10, then at most monthly: Keep / Quiet / Off for features you don't use.
learning.brain: The AI that looks at finished work; empty uses the concept graph's second-look AI, else your main one.
learning.corrections: When you correct a skill's answer, the skill keeps it as a lesson.
learning.remember: The nightly look back keeps facts you stated in your chats and calls in your how-to-help-me note.
learning.remember_max: The most facts kept in a night.
learning.search: A search index of past requests, calls and chats on this computer: `/history`, and the AI's search_history.
learning.skill_min_steps: How many tool uses a request needs before it's considered for a new skill.
learning.skills: A request that took many steps can become a skill, or improve the one that does it.
lidsafe.hours: How far ahead your call line holds reminders and the morning line, in hours.
lidsafe.morning: When the morning line comes if no wake-up alarm is set.
lidsafe.reminders: Your reminders still reach the phone while this computer is asleep or off.
lidsafe.today: A morning line on your phone with the day's first class and what's due, even with the lid shut.
local_helper.hold_h: Hours a request waits for the internet before it gives up and says so.
local_helper.max_s: How fast the helper must answer in its speed test (seconds), or it stays off.
local_helper.model: Which Ollama model the offline helper uses; empty picks the standard small one.
local_helper.offer: Offer the offline helper once if your free limit keeps running short or the internet often drops.
local_helper.offline: With the internet down: quick things answered here, AI requests wait in the queue until it's back.
local_helper.on: A small model on this computer (about 1 GB) for quick decisions and as a stand-in while the internet is down.
local_helper.timeout_s: Seconds a quick decision waits for the helper before the rules decide instead.
look.being_hints: The being's hints: what to click and what each part is (H on the board toggles them).
look.being_live_waveform: The being's YOU lane live: a trace of the microphone's loudness as you speak, the last six seconds.
look.being_mood: Brain's own mood in the drawing: the fluid's tint and the heart's beat; its pupil and pulse show the three knobs.
look.being_resting_sparks: The being's resting sparks: a low trickle in the brain from what Kurooto does all the time.
look.being_status: The being as a glance: eyes shut in focus or asleep, the held count by the heart, a glow on the deadline it's uneasy about.
look.being_theme: The being's colours: white light on black, or the page's palette.
look.board: The board: Kurooto as one living body (being), three panes on top (three), or STATUS on the left (classic).
look.brain_monitor: BRAIN's part monitor: shown beside the model, or in a drawer behind a tab.
look.chat_page: The Chat page (Alt+H): the phone app's chat on the dashboard, live, with its buttons, and a box to write in it.
look.design: The dashboard's design: new (sans-serif, rounded panes) or classic (the monospace look of 0.5.18).
look.hidden_features: Features hidden from the Features list (they still run if they're on).
look.layout: Dense (everything on one full-screen board) or roomy (bigger panes and type).
look.links_in: Where links to other sites open: this computer's default browser, or the browser showing the dashboard.
look.palette: The colours of Kurooto's pages and terminals: its own palettes, your desktop's, or a named theme.
look.panes: Panes hidden from the dense board: status, systems, notes, terminal.
look.projects: Folders of git repositories the PROJECTS box shows; empty uses Research's repositories.
look.settings_guide: On the Settings page, a line under each setting that says what it does and opens its whole guide entry.
look.study_mode: The dashboard in Study mode: the notes map, the study timer and what's due (Alt+M, `/study mode`).
look.talk_box: A small box over the board to talk to Kurooto in plain English (Alt+K).
look.theme_file: A colours file of your own (a kitty theme, or matugen or pywal JSON) instead of the desktop's.
mail_digest.at: When the mail digest checks your Gmail.
mail_digest.confidential: What happens to confidential mail: only counted, or summarised by a model on this computer.
mail_digest.confidential_words: The markings that make a mail confidential (in its subject, text or a label).
mail_digest.first_days: How far back (days) the first digest looks.
mail_digest.local_model: Which Ollama model summarises confidential mail; empty uses Local AI models' helper.
mail_digest.mail_in: Email in: mail you forward to you+kurooto@ (or label) is filed into your notes, its dates as buttons.
mail_digest.mail_in_anyone: Mail to +kurooto from anyone goes in. A stranger could then write into your notes.
mail_digest.mail_in_every: How often Gmail is checked for mail you sent in.
mail_digest.mail_in_label: A Gmail label whose mail goes into your notes too, from anyone.
mail_digest.mail_in_senders: Your other email addresses that may send mail into your notes (your own always can).
mail_digest.max_messages: The most mails looked at per check.
mail_digest.never_read: Senders, @domains or labels the digest never reads, even if chosen elsewhere.
mail_digest.own_domain: On a school or work account, mail from your own organisation's domain is read too.
mail_digest.query: A Gmail search: mail it matches is read too, e.g. everything but Promotions and Social.
mail_digest.read: What the AI may read for the digest: senders, @domains or Gmail labels you chose.
mail_digest.save_note: A copy of each digest goes into your notes (mail/).
mail_digest.skip_confidential: Mail marked confidential is only counted: never read by the AI, summarised or answered.
meetings.after_h: Hours after a meeting's start that a voice note or long note counts as notes from it.
meetings.minutes: Notes you send after a meeting with a project's person become minutes, through your AI.
memory.budget_tokens: At most about this much of what's remembered goes with one reply or call (about 4 characters a token).
memory.recall: Replies and calls are told the few remembered items your message refers to ("as we said on the call").
memory.thread_days: Days an untouched open thread waits before it closes by itself.
memory.threads: What you say you'll do, and tasks you start, become open threads ("did I finish that thing?").
mind.act: More of what Brain proposes is decided by its trust: below the bar it asks, above it acts and tells, with Undo.
mind.act.more: Its trust decides study blocks, reshaped plans, revision packs and keeping its night's cards and lines.
mind.anchor_every: How often (in records) Brain notes where its log has got to, besides once a day.
mind.attention: A model of Brain's own attention, for "what are you thinking about?".
mind.attention.on: A model of its own attention: "what are you thinking about?" is answered from it.
mind.autonomy: What Brain may do without asking, learned per kind of action from your reactions.
mind.autonomy.enforce: Make its trust verdicts bind: it asks first for what it isn't trusted with.
mind.autonomy.on: Brain learns from your reactions how far it may act on its own, per class of action (shadow first).
mind.autonomy.shadow_days: Days its trust verdicts are only counted and shown, not used.
mind.autonomy.thresholds: Your own trust bars per class of action, over the defaults.
mind.backfill: Feeding Brain its past: what Kurooto kept before Brain was on, read once, source by source.
mind.backfill.calls: Read past calls (answered or missed, who placed them, how long), never what was said.
mind.backfill.checkins: Read which check-ins were asked, answered or skipped each day, never what you said.
mind.backfill.deadlines: Read when past deadlines were due and done (no titles).
mind.backfill.events: Read Kurooto's own event history: what happened and when.
mind.backfill.jobs: Read the AI request history: effort, whether it worked, how long (never the words).
mind.backfill.learning: Read how many requests and calls a day were indexed (chats left out).
mind.backfill.on: Brain reads what Kurooto kept before it was on, once (`/mind backfill`); off until you turn it on.
mind.backfill.quiz: Read your quiz record per day and subject (asked, right, wrong), never the questions.
mind.backfill.study: Read the study tracker's time per day, for your real pace in week plans.
mind.beliefs: Where each of Brain's beliefs came from, and how sure it is.
mind.beliefs.on: Keep where each belief came from (said, saw, inferred, imagined) and how sure it is.
mind.budget: Brain's body budget: what it keeps level about itself, and its drive.
mind.budget.on: The body budget: a few things about Kurooto's own state it tries to keep level, and its drive.
mind.checkins: Check-ins that come early when the day departs from Brain's forecast.
mind.checkins.surprise: The next check-in comes early when the day departs strongly from Brain's forecast.
mind.console: The Brain console: what the Brain decided and why, on the dashboard (Alt+O) and in the phone's Views.
mind.console.on: The Brain console: a dashboard page (Alt+O) and the phone's Brain view showing what the Brain decided and why.
mind.context: Brain's hints in every AI request: concepts you're shaky on and what's on its mind, never how you are.
mind.context.on: Every AI request gets Brain's hints: concepts you're shaky on, and what's on its mind.
mind.dream: Brain dreaming about the day: quiz cards, how-to-help lines and a voice line in the morning message.
mind.dream.cards: Each night, 1 to 3 quiz cards for concepts you studied that day that are on your frontier, kept by a tap.
mind.dream.cards_max: The most dream cards a night (1 to 3).
mind.dream.lessons: Each night, 1 to 3 lines for your how-to-help-me note from the day's outcomes, written only when you tap Keep.
mind.dream.on: Brain goes over the day at night and brings cards, how-to-help lines and a voice line to the morning message.
mind.dream.voice: One morning line on what the nightly voice learning saw: turns it learned from and any misfire pattern.
mind.expect: What Kurooto expects of each message it starts, and what came of it.
mind.expect.on: Each message Kurooto starts says what it expects (a reply, or done within 2 hours), and what came of it is recorded.
mind.feelings: Brain's feelings about specific things, its mood, and whether it may say them.
mind.feelings.empathy: Concern for what it looks after (deadlines, projects, its machine): it notices sooner, speaks more gently.
mind.feelings.express: Brain may say a feeling about something open, through the gate, at most 3 times a week unasked.
mind.feelings.mood: Its mood shapes it: low, it does less unasked, asks first, says less; high, a little bolder.
mind.feelings.on: Brain's states about specific things (uneasy, relieved…) and what they make it do inwardly.
mind.feelings.vocal: Let Brain say unasked that it's excited or worried, when it has strong evidence.
mind.finetune: A weekly local fine-tune of the model on this computer, from checked examples only.
mind.finetune.base: The local model's name in Ollama to build the adapter into; empty is the helper model.
mind.finetune.base_hf: The Hugging Face name of the base model, which the trainer loads.
mind.finetune.day: The night of the week it trains.
mind.finetune.min_examples: With fewer checked examples than this, it skips the week.
mind.finetune.on: A weekly local fine-tune of the model on this computer, from checked examples only.
mind.finetune.practice: Include the harness' practice tasks in training.
mind.finetune.probe_words: Words of a forgotten prompt kept to check a new adapter forgot it (3 or more).
mind.forecast: What Brain expects of tomorrow, scored the next evening.
mind.forecast.holdout: The share of days a planned action is held back on purpose, to measure what it does.
mind.forecast.on: Each evening at 21:00, what Brain expects of tomorrow, scored the next evening.
mind.forget: How old things fade from use, old misses stop coming up, and a forget reaches everywhere.
mind.forget.half_lives: Days for each kind of memory to fade to half.
mind.forget.half_lives.default: Days for a remembered item to fade to half, when its kind has no own setting.
mind.forget.half_lives.fact: Days for a fact about you to fade to half.
mind.forget.half_lives.gist: Days for a conversation's gist to fade to half.
mind.forget.half_lives.project: Days for a project fact to fade to half.
mind.forget.misses_weeks: After this many weeks, a past miss is no longer brought up.
mind.forget.on: Old things fade from use, old misses stop coming up, and `/forget` goes everywhere Brain kept something.
mind.gate: Brain's gate on what reaches you: limits, honest feelings, small touches.
mind.gate.feelings_per_week: How often Brain may say how it feels about something unasked, per week.
mind.gate.max_per_day: Messages a day that may come by themselves (Calm's limit applies too: the smaller wins).
mind.gate.max_per_hour: Messages an hour that may come by themselves.
mind.gate.on: Brain's gate on everything Kurooto sends by itself: only ever quieter, honest feelings, a shared pool of small touches.
mind.gate.touches_per_day: Small human touches a day in all (an absence note, a lighter-day line, a feeling).
mind.hardened: The scorekeeper runs as its own system user, so not even a program running as you can change the log.
mind.harness: The hidden harness: tasks it has never seen, to measure whether it's getting better.
mind.harness.on: Nightly on the charger: how it does on tasks it has never seen, and checks of Brain's own promises.
mind.harness.rotate_days: The hidden tasks are made new this often (days), so old ones can't be memorised.
mind.heartbeat: What your call line says has no guarantee while this computer is down.
mind.heartbeat.on: When this computer is down, your call line also says what the next 12 hours have no guarantee for.
mind.improve: Brain improving itself, only through gated proposals you approve.
mind.improve.on: Brain improving itself through gated proposals: nothing changes without the hidden harness and your say-so.
mind.journal: Brain's daily journal of its own states and mistakes, and its copy in your notes.
mind.journal.in_notes: Also keep Brain's journal as a block in a note of yours.
mind.journal.in_notes_file: The journal note's file name (`.md` is added if missing).
mind.journal.in_notes_folder: The folder inside your notes the journal note goes in; empty is the top.
mind.journal.on: A daily journal of Brain's own states, reasons and mistakes, every line checked against its log.
mind.knobs: Three honest knobs: its mood sets exploration, arousal how soon it speaks up, calibration whether it asks.
mind.knobs.on: Three knobs: its mood sets how much it explores, arousal how soon it speaks up, calibration whether it asks first.
mind.lab: The overnight lab: pre-registered experiments on projects you list.
mind.lab.gpu: Let lab runs use the graphics card (off: CPU only).
mind.lab.gpu_hours_per_night: The most graphics-card hours the lab uses in a night.
mind.lab.in_repo: Keep a project's lab protocol in its `.kurooto` folder (off: in Kurooto's own state).
mind.lab.max_per_night: The most configurations in one night's batch.
mind.lab.on: Overnight pre-registered experiments on the projects you list (Linux and macOS, in a sandbox).
mind.lab.projects: Folders (or repository projects' names) the lab may run experiments on.
mind.lab.run_wall_s: Seconds one lab run may take before it's stopped.
mind.lab.seed: A fixed seed for the sampled configurations; 0 draws a new sample each day.
mind.pest: Whether each kind of unprompted message is welcome, learned from your reactions.
mind.pest.on: Learn for each kind of unprompted message whether it's welcome; send one only when it likely is.
mind.plans.on: Plans over weeks: which milestones are at risk, from simulated futures. A suggestion, never a push.
mind.plans.rollouts: How many simulated futures a plan runs.
mind.plans.weeks: How far ahead (weeks) the simulated futures look.
mind.play: A little nightly time for Brain to explore its own questions on your topics.
mind.play.minutes_per_night: Minutes of play a night, on the charger only.
mind.play.on: A little nightly time to explore its own questions on your topics (off until you turn it on).
mind.precedents: Judgement calls between your values, asked once and then followed.
mind.precedents.on: Judgement calls between your values are asked once, then followed (off until you turn it on).
mind.precedents.threshold: How alike two situations must be (0 to 1) for a precedent to be followed.
mind.presence_forecast: When you'll be at your desk and free, forecast hours ahead and paid only for being right.
mind.presence_forecast.on: Forecast, hour by hour for the next six hours, when you'll be at your desk and free; scored against what the senses then show.
mind.presence_forecast.prefer: Check-ins and calls Kurooto places by itself prefer an hour you're likely free.
mind.presence_forecast.within_min: How far (minutes) a check-in or a call may move to a likelier hour.
mind.promises: Brain's own promises: kept, or owned up to first.
mind.promises.on: Its own promises ("I'll check back at 6") are noticed, kept, or owned up to first.
mind.read: Brain's read of how you're doing.
mind.read.asks_per_week: How many times a week, at most, it may ask whether the week felt heavier than usual.
mind.read.on: Brain's read of how you're doing, from numbers about your days; in shadow mode it only watches.
mind.register: One temperament from its mood and arousal: how long its unprompted words are, and Voice's pace for them.
mind.register.on: One temperament: its mood and arousal set how long its unprompted words are, its call openers and Voice's pace.
mind.register.templates: Its ready-made unprompted messages keep the register's 2, 3 or 4 sentences too, not only what the AI writes.
mind.senses: What Brain senses: its own machine, your activity, your phone's sensors.
mind.senses.activity: The activity stream: the app in front, hashed window titles, saves and commits (never keystrokes, the screen or URLs).
mind.senses.intero: Its own machine's state every minute: temperatures, memory, battery, disk, AI limits.
mind.senses.phone: Each of your phone's sensors, off until you switch it on (here and in the phone app).
mind.skills: Skills Brain learns from solved tasks and from what you repeat.
mind.skills.from_demos: Also offer skills from what you do over and over (asked once).
mind.skills.on: Solved tasks become tested, reusable skills; each new one starts out asking first.
mind.sleep: Kurooto's sleep: when it doesn't talk unless woken, following your night.
mind.sleep.desk_after_min: With desk_holds: how many minutes after you leave the desk its sleep starts.
mind.sleep.desk_holds: While you're at this computer, Kurooto doesn't fall asleep: its night starts after you leave.
mind.sleep.follow_owner: Its sleep follows yours: bedtime to the alarm, refined by your phone (screen off, dark, charging; first use).
mind.sleep.on: Kurooto sleeps in your sleep window: nothing it starts by itself is sent or said aloud until morning.
mind.sleep.senses_off: Asleep, Kurooto's camera and microphone are off: Face presence pauses and Voice stops listening.
mind.sleep.wake_minutes: Woken by its name or a message at night, it dozes off again after this many quiet minutes.
mind.sleep.window: Set Kurooto's sleep by hand, like 00:30-08:00 (empty: follow your night).
mind.status: One status stream for every face of Brain: the being, the phone's Views, Voice and add-ons.
mind.status.on: One status stream: focus, asleep, messages held, the one thing it's uneasy about, its own mood and arousal.
mind.stimulation: Brain's senses felt as a body, for its feelings and the dashboard.
mind.stimulation.addons: Let an add-on feed another device's sensors into its body (light, motion, battery, loudness...).
mind.stimulation.jolt: Something sudden (a pickup, something close, a loud room) is felt at once: a jolt, and a fresh look at its mind.
mind.stimulation.on: Its senses felt as a body (heat, load, touch), for its feelings and the dashboard.
mind.story: The life story every part of Kurooto starts from.
mind.story.on: One life story every part of Kurooto reads first: a fixed core, then its recent weeks.
mind.story.tokens: The life story's summary is at most this many tokens (about 4 characters each).
mind.study_push: One morning line about the subject Brain is most uneasy about, in place of its separate nudges.
mind.study_push.horizon_days: How far ahead a deadline can be for Brain to be uneasy about it.
mind.study_push.minutes: How long a study stretch the morning line offers.
mind.study_push.on: One morning line about the subject Brain is most uneasy about (due date, minutes logged, cards due), with Yes and Later.
mind.talk: Whether being talked to is a small reward for Brain.
mind.talk.met: An add-on's chat with someone in the room is a smaller reward for Brain (at most 0.05 a day, 6 meetings).
mind.talk.on: Being talked to is a small reward for Brain (at most 0.2 a day; nothing for answers to its own pings).
mind.tom: Brain's model of what you know, believe and want.
mind.tom.attention: Hold a message (at most 15 minutes) while you're deep in one project.
mind.tom.false_beliefs: When something you were told turns out wrong, tell you once, with the evidence.
mind.tom.on: A model of what you know, believe, want and prefer, each row with its source (`/model`).
mind.tone: One-word tone tags on what you write, from the model on this computer only.
mind.tone.on: Tag each message you write with one word (calm, tired…), using the model on this computer only.
mind.values: What Brain learns to value, in shadow first.
mind.values.on: Brain learns which kinds of things help (values), never affecting a choice in the shadow days.
mind.values.shadow_days: Days learned values are only counted, never used for a choice.
mind.why: "Why this?" under a message Kurooto started.
mind.why.on: "Why this?" under a message Kurooto started says what Brain's gate and door did with it, what it expected, and how many it has sent today.
mind.why.to_ai: A message that asks why also gives your AI the plain reasons for Kurooto's own last few messages.
mind.workspace: The small "now" stage that decides what's on Brain's mind.
mind.workspace.arbiter: One door for everything Kurooto says by itself: each message bids, and only winners are sent.
mind.workspace.break_after_min: Minutes in one window before switching to another counts as a natural break.
mind.workspace.breaks: A winner that isn't urgent waits for a natural break: a window switch after a long stretch, a phone pickup, a session ending.
mind.workspace.capacity: How many things can be on Brain's mind at once (1 to 3).
mind.workspace.cycle_s: The least gap in seconds between two cycles (events poke it sooner).
mind.workspace.fold_h: Hours a message may keep losing at the door before it goes into the evening bundle instead.
mind.workspace.max_hold_min: The longest a winner waits for a break, in minutes (unless Kurooto is asleep).
mind.workspace.on: A small "now" stage that parts compete to enter; only what wins may start a message or act on its own.
mind.yield: The Brain's heavy work yields to yours: the graphics card, calls, battery, heat.
mind.yield.on: The Brain's heavy work waits while your jobs use the graphics card, during a call, on battery or when hot.
mind.yield.prefer_sleep: The Brain's nightly work also waits for Kurooto to be asleep (until that night's window ends).
modules.enabled: The features that are on. The Features page changes it.
notes.layout: How your notes folder is laid out: Kurooto's folders, or a Zettelkasten.
notes.links: How Kurooto links notes: `[[wikilinks]]` or Markdown links.
notes.open_with: The program that opens a note from the dashboard; empty uses the system's.
notes.paths: Your own place for a kind of note, over the layout's.
notes_sync.after_jobs: Minutes after an AI request finishes that the notes it wrote go up; 0 waits for the timer.
notes_sync.api: The Git host's API address. Leave it alone.
notes_sync.branch: The branch your notes sync to (filled in from the repository).
